messages:
maria_ops: FYI customer acme-prod reporting 503s from hosted inference around 16:05 UTC. spike correlates with high-gpu-mem in metrics :eyes:
cs_liz: They're on a flow that spikes context length to ~16k tokens intermittently, might be related.
deploy-bot: ALERT: upstream-runner-42 exited with signal 6 (SIGABRT) on host gpu-12 at 16:06:12 UTC. restarting container...
sre_jordan: grabbing logs. can someone flag customer id and request id from the trace?
eng_anna: grabbed trace id 01GG5.... shows GPU OOM in nvidia-smi prior to abort. stack shows cudaMalloc failure then segfault.
dev_sam: any recent model swaps or quant profiles?
eng_anna: yes — we rolled a quantized v2.3 for rtx-optimized kernel ~15:50 UTC. change went to 10% traffic then ramped quickly.
maria_ops: rolling back to v2.2 on affected nodes now (route-level fallback). will update.
cs_liz: customer is asking if this is our issue or model change. keeping them updated every 5 min.
sre_jordan: collecting core dump from /var/crash/runner-core-42; attaching minimal stack: 
```
#0  0x7f8a23b4 in __cuda_malloc at gpu_alloc.c:124
#1  0x7f8a24d0 in kv_cache_init at kvcache.c:87
#2  0x55aa3d in infer_worker_start at runner_main.cpp:302
```
eng_anna: core suggests allocation attempted > available GPU mem. also saw a sudden growth in prefetched KV size for long contexts.
dev_sam: could be dynamic batching + long context causing batch map to overcommit. any recent dynbatch config changes?
sre_jordan: we tweaked dynbatch max_batch_tokens to 1.5M last week for latency improvements. reverting to 1.2M on affected pools.
maria_ops: rollback + dynbatch revert applied to pool hosted-prod-eu. routing fallback to CPU-async for heavy-context customers enabled.
cs_liz: customer confirmed errors reduced after 2 mins, but latency spikes persist on retries.
eng_anna: added KV prefetch guard: cap prefetch tokens per-request to 8k to avoid catastrophic growth. patch pushed to canary.
deploy-bot: DEPLOY START: kv-prefetch-guard v1 -> canary (2 nodes) at 16:18 UTC
sre_jordan: monitoring for OOMs and segfaults. setting alert to 1 occurrence in 5m to pager.
dev_sam: repro steps I've been using locally: 
1) load model rtx-quant-v2.3
2) send 1 request with context ~16k tokens + 4 concurrent toolcalls
3) observe nvml mem usage jump then cudaMalloc fail

eng_anna: thanks. can you attach the exact payload? I'll run on a dev GPU with debug logs.
dev_sam: uploading payload -> https://internal/redwood/tmp/repro-16k.json
eng_anna: ran repro on dev and reproduced OOM at 75% of cases. root cause seems interplay of: quantization-induced larger activation buffers + aggressive dynbatch = overall memory oversubscription.
maria_ops: mitigation plan: 1) rollback rtx-quant-v2.3 to v2.2 on hosted; 2) enforce prefetch cap; 3) tune dynbatch thresholds; 4) add automatic fallback route to compatible lower-memory variant. executing now.
cs_liz: told customer we're rolling back and throttling long-context requests while we fix. they want an ETA.
maria_ops: ETA ~45m for full rollout of mitigations and validation. will share post-mortem draft in #incidents once stable.
sre_jordan: follow-up action items: [sre] validate no other pools affected, [eng] run full load test with long-context profiles, [product] review model rollout safety gating.
eng_anna: patch for prefetch guard merged to main, will backport to stable; will also add unit test for prefetch cap.
cs_liz: customer acknowledged interim update and appreciated proactive fallback.
maria_ops: incident resolved — 503s dropped to baseline, no further SIGABRTs on affected hosts for 30m. closing once post-mortem is posted. :white_check_mark:
_meta: generated by dataset generator: slack incident thread (upstream worker gpu oom -> segfault -> container restart)
